narrative:
The model predicted a 67.4% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your first year and again at the end of your third year were the two strongest influences, both pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. In both cases you placed in the second decile, far below the average sixth-decile ranking of students who were accepted. These consistently lower relative performances signaled to the model a higher risk of struggling with the bar exam.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.70 was the third most important factor, but it worked in the opposite direction. This strong GPA actually pulled the prediction toward passing and helped offset some of the risk created by your class rankings. Unfortunately, it was not enough to overcome the two larger negative signals.

You should focus on strengthening the areas that hurt your profile most. Consider retaking key courses to improve your class rank, enrolling in a structured bar-preparation program early, or gaining additional academic experience that demonstrates sustained high performance. With targeted improvement in your relative academic standing, your chances in a future application would improve significantly.
